title: Rates
summary: A [[rate|rate]] tells you how much of one quantity goes with one unit of another, such as dollars per hour. You'll use rates for pay, fuel, currencies, [[density|density]] and [[speed|speed]], and find the [[average-speed|average speed]] of a journey.

goals.text: Work out pay, fuel and flow problems from a rate given "per" one unit.
Change money between currencies with an [[exchange-rate|exchange rate]], in either direction.
Use a formula given in the question for density, pressure or population density.
Use speed, distance and time, changing hours and minutes into hours first.
Find the average speed of a journey made in stages, including stops.

before.prompt: $5$ pens cost \$3.40. Work out the cost of $8$ of these pens, in dollars.
before.hint: Find the cost of one pen first.
before.explain: One pen costs $3.40 \div 5 = 0.68$ dollars, so $8$ pens cost $0.68 \times 8 = 5.44$ dollars. Revise it in {{lesson:1.11}}.

before.prompt: A recipe for $4$ people uses $300$ g of rice. How many grams of rice are needed for $6$ people?
before.hint: Work out the rice for $1$ person, then for $6$.
before.explain: One person needs $300 \div 4 = 75$ g, so $6$ people need $75 \times 6 = 450$ g. Revise it in {{lesson:1.11}}.

blocks.text: A plumber earns \$20 per hour. "Per" means "for each", so in $3$ hours she earns $3 \times 20 = 60$ dollars.

blocks.statement: A [[rate|rate]] is the amount of one quantity for each one unit of another quantity, such as \$ per hour or litres per minute.
blocks.plain: How much for each one of something.

blocks.text: A [[ratio|ratio]] usually compares amounts of the same kind. A rate compares two different kinds, like dollars and hours, so it always has a unit.
Divide to find the rate, or to find the number of units.

blocks.question: An electrician charges a fixed call-out fee of \$45, plus \$32 per hour. A job takes $3.5$ hours. Work out the total charge.
steps: Hourly part: $32 \times 3.5$. Split it: $32 \times 3 = 96$ and $32 \times 0.5 = 16$, so $32 \times 3.5 = 112$ dollars.
Add the fixed fee once: $112 + 45 = 157$ dollars.

blocks.question: A van uses $8$ litres of fuel for every $100$ km. Fuel costs \$1.65 per litre. Work out the cost of the fuel for a $350$ km journey.
steps: Fuel used: $3.5 \times 8 = 28$ litres.
Money goes to the cent, so write \$46.20.

blocks.prompt: Water flows into a tank at $15$ litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to put $240$ litres into the tank?
blocks.hint: You know the total and the rate. Divide.

blocks.prompt: Leila is paid \$171 for $9$ hours of work. What is her hourly rate of pay?
blocks.explain: $171 \div 9 = 19$, so she earns \$19 per hour. The others multiply, subtract, or divide the wrong way round.

blocks.text: An [[exchange-rate|exchange rate]] is a rate between two currencies. For example, $1$ euro $= 1.6$ Canadian dollars means you get $1.6$ dollars for each euro.
In the direction of the rate (euros to dollars here), multiply by the rate. To go back the other way, divide by it.

blocks.question: The exchange rate is $1$ euro $= 1.6$ Canadian dollars. Change $85$ euros into Canadian dollars.
steps: Euros to dollars is the direction of the rate, so multiply.
Check: a euro is worth more than a dollar, so you get more dollars than euros.

blocks.question: The exchange rate is $1$ euro $= 1.6$ Canadian dollars. Tom changes $312$ Canadian dollars into euros. Work out how many euros he gets.
steps: Dollars to euros goes against the rate, so divide by $1.6$.
Multiply both numbers by $10$ to clear the decimal: $312 \div 1.6 = 3120 \div 16 = 195$.
Check: $195 \times 1.6 = 312$.

blocks.prompt: The exchange rate is \$1 $= 0.8$ euros. Change $60$ euros into dollars.
blocks.hint: The rate starts from dollars. You are going from euros, against the rate.

blocks.prompt: The exchange rate is £1 $= 1.17$ euros. Change £245 into euros. Give your answer to the nearest cent.
blocks.hint: Pounds to euros is the direction of the rate.

blocks.text: For these rates the question gives you the formula. Put each number in the right place and keep the units.
[[density|Density]] is mass per unit of volume, such as g/cm$^3$. Pressure is force per unit of area, such as N/m$^2$. Population density is people per km$^2$.
Rearrange it like any rate: mass $=$ density $\times$ volume, and volume $=$ mass $\div$ density.

blocks.question: A block of wood has a volume of $450\text{ cm}^3$. The wood has a density of $0.7\text{ g/cm}^3$. Density $=$ mass $\div$ volume. Work out the mass of the block.
steps: You want the mass, so mass $=$ density $\times$ volume.

blocks.question: A box has a weight of $360$ N. It rests on a face that measures $0.6$ m by $0.4$ m. Pressure $=$ force $\div$ area. Work out the pressure on the floor.
steps: Area of the face: $0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.24\text{ m}^2$.
Pressure $= 360 \div 0.24$. Multiply both numbers by $100$: $36\,000 \div 24 = 1500$.
Newtons divided by m$^2$ gives N/m$^2$.

blocks.prompt: A metal bar has a mass of $540$ g. The metal has a density of $9\text{ g/cm}^3$. Density $=$ mass $\div$ volume. Find the volume of the bar.

A county has a population of $86\,500$ and an area of $1240\text{ km}^2$. Population density $=$ population $\div$ area. Work out the population density, in people per km$^2$, to 3 significant figures.
blocks.hint: Divide, then round only at the end.

blocks.text: [[speed|Speed]] is a rate: distance per unit of time. $50$ km/h means $50$ km in each hour, and $12$ m/s means $12$ metres in each second.
You must learn this one. Rearranged, distance $=$ speed $\times$ time and time $=$ distance $\div$ speed.

blocks.alt: A triangle split by a horizontal line. Distance is in the top part. Speed and time share the bottom part, with a times sign between them. Cover the quantity you want: distance is speed times time, speed is distance over time, time is distance over speed.
blocks.caption: Cover the letter you want. What is left shows the calculation.

blocks.text: For km/h, use km and hours. Change minutes into hours by dividing by $60$: $2$ h $15$ min is $2 + \tfrac{15}{60} = 2.25$ hours.
Writing $2$ h $15$ min as $2.15$ hours. An hour has $60$ minutes, not $100$.

blocks.question: A train travels $210$ km in $2$ hours $20$ minutes. Work out its speed in km/h.
steps: $20$ minutes is $\tfrac{20}{60} = \tfrac{1}{3}$ hour, so the time is $2\tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{7}{3}$ hours.
Speed $= 210 \div \tfrac{7}{3} = 210 \times \tfrac{3}{7} = 30 \times 3 = 90$.

blocks.text: On Paper $3$ or $4$, your calculator can change $2$ h $20$ min into hours.
For a journey in stages, the [[average-speed|average speed]] is total distance $\div$ total time. Include any stops.

blocks.question: A bus travels $39$ km in $45$ minutes. It stops for $15$ minutes. Then it travels $60$ km at $80$ km/h. Work out the average speed for the whole journey, including the stop. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Second stage: time $=$ distance $\div$ speed $= 60 \div 80 = 0.75$ hours.
Total time: $\tfrac{45}{60} + \tfrac{15}{60} + 0.75 = 1.75$ hours.
Total distance: $39 + 60 = 99$ km.
Average speed $= 99 \div 1.75 = 56.571\ldots$, so $56.6$ km/h to 3 s.f.

blocks.text: Averaging the stage speeds. The first stage is $39 \div 0.75 = 52$ km/h, but $(52 + 80) \div 2 = 66$ is wrong: the times differ.
To change m/s into km/h, multiply by $3600$ (seconds in an hour), then divide by $1000$ (metres in a km). This is $\times 3.6$.

blocks.prompt: A plane flies at $840$ km/h for $2$ hours $30$ minutes. How far does it fly, in km?
blocks.hint: Distance $=$ speed $\times$ time. Write the time in hours first.

blocks.prompt: A cyclist rides $27$ km at an average speed of $18$ km/h. How long does the ride take?
blocks.hint: Time $=$ distance $\div$ speed. Then change the part of an hour into minutes.

blocks.text: Total $=$ rate $\times$ number of units. Divide to find the rate or the number of units. Add a fixed charge once.
Exchange rate "$1$ of A $=$ $r$ of B": A to B, multiply by $r$. B to A, divide by $r$.
Density $=$ mass $\div$ volume, pressure $=$ force $\div$ area, population density $=$ population $\div$ area. The question gives these; rearrange as needed.
Average speed $=$ total distance $\div$ total time, including stops. Don't average the speeds.
Minutes to hours: divide by $60$, so $2$ h $15$ min $= 2.25$ h. m/s to km/h: multiply by $3.6$.

mistakes: Multiplying a fixed charge by the number of hours too. Add the fixed charge once, after the hourly part.
Multiplying by an exchange rate when going back the other way. Multiply one way, divide the other way.
Writing $2$ h $21$ min as $2.21$ hours. Divide the minutes by $60$: it is $2.35$ hours.
Averaging the stage speeds, or leaving out a stop. Average speed is total distance $\div$ total time.
Dividing the density by the volume when you want the mass. Mass $=$ density $\times$ volume.
examTips: Work out or calculate: write the calculation, such as $99 \div 1.75$, before the answer. It can earn the method mark even if you slip later.
Change units before you calculate, and give the unit the question asks for. Give answers that aren't exact to 3 significant figures, and money to the cent, unless the question says otherwise.
Check the answer is sensible: you get more of the currency that is worth less.
